set.approach: Access is a flight to Qikiqtarjuaq, then a chartered boat or a sea kayak trip from there. From the coast, follow the north arm of the Coronation Glacier up. The line starts where rock emerges from the ice on the glacier's north margin.
set.descent_text: The way down from the top follows the rim of the canyon west and northwest, then descends into the upper end of the obvious river valley toward a tributary glacier. Where that glacier meets the main glacier there is an impassable canyon, so the line returns uphill and handrails the cliff west of the tributary glacier above unstable ice-cored moraine. A prominent bowl east of the climb may offer another way down.

review.notes: Route page states approach and the descent line used on the first ascent; stated as terrain, hazards kept.

set.approach: Access is a flight to Qikiqtarjuaq, then a chartered boat or a sea kayak trip from there. Follow the north arm of the Coronation Glacier up. The line starts where rock emerges from the ice on the glacier's north margin, and a water-filled moat separates the rock from the ice; crossing it takes a swim in a dry suit or a Tyrolean traverse rigged from the far side.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappelling the route with two ropes, from gear anchors, slung horns and one single-bolt anchor, so carry extra gear to supplement them. A walk-off may be possible down one of several gullies west of the route.

review.notes: Route page; rappel count left out (single source).

set.approach: Access is a flight to Qikiqtarjuaq, then a chartered boat or a sea kayak trip from there. The route climbs the prominent ridge and buttress on the north side of the Coronation Glacier, just downstream of the split between its north and south arms. The approach begins at the bottom of the low ridge leading to the buttress: climb the bowl on the right side of that ridge and reach the ridge higher up by way of fourth-class ramps.
set.descent_text: From the top head north across the summit plateau, then trend down and to the left over wide talus and slab fields above a cliff band. A fourth-class chimney leads down through the cliff band, and from there the route exits back right out of the river valley onto the Coronation Glacier.

review.notes: Route page states approach and descent.

set.approach: Walk northeast up the Weasel River valley from Thor Shelter, toward the end of the cliff and stopping short of the last major waterfall, which falls between Mount Northumbria and the unnamed mountain to its northeast. The route follows a corner system a short way to the right of that waterfall, on the buttress at the far right (east) end of the crag.
set.descent_text: Descent is by rappel down the route, using slings on boulders at the first stations, then nut anchors and a cordelette on a boulder; the lowest section can instead be downclimbed on climber's right.

review.notes: Route page; rappel count and times left out (single source).

set.approach: Walk northeast up the Weasel River valley from Thor Shelter along the hiking trail; the first climbs are at the southwest end of the wall. Birthday Crack is a short finger crack beside the neighboring easy line.

set.approach: Walk northeast up the Weasel River valley from Thor Shelter, toward the end of the cliff and stopping short of the last major waterfall, which falls between Mount Northumbria and the unnamed mountain to its northeast. The line starts on thin cracks and slabs that lead to layback corners next to the waterfall.
set.descent_text: Descent is by the same rappel line used for the neighboring route Aalaapi, down to the base.

review.notes: Route page states 'same rap as Aalaapi'; the Aalaapi page was read only to confirm what that line is.

set.approach: From the Thor emergency shelter, hike up the valley on the trail, then leave it and go up gentle scree to the bottom-most outcrop on the west side of the Weasel Valley. The route starts at an obvious broken crack there, and the wishbone-shaped crack on the fourth pitch is the landmark of the line. The brown slabs above are cut by many splitter cracks.
set.descent_text: Descent is by double-rope rappels straight down the route, swinging around the corner to the top of the fourth pitch, then a walk-off down a large ramp splitting the first two pitches. From the fixed anchor near the top it is also possible to traverse out right to walk off, or left toward Mount Northumbria.

review.notes: Single route page read in full; rappel count left out. Found via photo breadcrumbs on the Thor Shelter Crag area.
